newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK Sept industry output seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK Sept industry output seen rebounding.

text.p: UK September industrial production data, due on Tuesday, are likely to show a rebound after the unexpected decline seen in August, economists said.

Leading business surveys point to a pickup in output, stocks appear to be falling and manufacturers themselves expect buoyant consumer spending to translate into increased orders in the coming months. The Reuters consensus forecast is for industrial production to rise 0.5 percent month/month and 0.2 percent year/year in September. August saw a monthly fall of 0.4 percent.
Manufacturing output is expected to grow 0.5 percent month/month and 0.1 percent year/year. In August it fell 0.3 percent from the previous month.
Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets, says August showed manufacturers were not out of the woods yet, but he believes the setback will prove temporary.
"With the stock overhang shrinking, stronger demand and greater optimism has been reflected in a sharp rise in output expectations," he said.

"September's figures could herald the beginnings of the recovery. We expect a 1/2 percent month-on-month rise in manufacturing output, lifting the annual rate back into positive territory at +0.2 percent and bringing an end to the technical recession seen in manufacturing in the last three quarters."
But Loynes added that the recovery is likely to look fragile for some time, "with a further rise in sterling threatening to dampen activity before it really starts to accelerate."
David Philpotts of Schroders expects the bounce-back in September production to reflect strong domestic orders rather than a pickup in export demand.
"In fact, the recovery from recession has almost entirely been a domestic story, suggesting growth is assured regardless of sterling's recent behaviour," he wrote in a commentary.
"Nevertheless, the deterioration in export competitiveness (albeit from a very strong starting point) is a reason to modestly pare back forecasts for industrial production next year."
Michael Saunders of Salomon Brothers said the August data were hit by lower oil output and a dip in manufacturing, largely reflecting lower output of the engineering sector.

"We expect both sectors to rebound in September. Business surveys suggest that the trend in manufacturing output has improved markedly in recent months, with a sharp upturn in figures from both the CBI and purchasing managers," he wrote in his Sterling Weekly.

Philip Uglow of Union Discount expects manufacturing to have emerged from recession in the third quarter as a whole and says he is cautiously optimistic about the sector. But he does have some concerns about stocks.

"Despite a 215 million stg reduction in inventories in Q2, the stock/output ratio remains high and is still likely to act as a restraining force on the pace of expansion over the coming months," he said. "Bearing this in mind, we expect to see moderate and not booming growth over the next few months."
For September, Uglow is forecasting a rise in manufacturing output of 0.4 percent month/month and 0.1 percent year/year, with overall production up 0.6 percent and 0.1 percent respectively.
